web_title: 8. Stage 3 Technical Structure, Institutional Flow & Upward-Only Stop Ratchet
book_title: Chapter 8: Reading the Tape — Stage 3 Consolidation, Volume & Structural Floor
question: What does the slip into Stan Weinstein Stage 3 below the 50-day SMA and 10-week EMA tell us about institutional demand, and how do we reconcile TradingView's raw support band (₹1,597–₹1,646) with our locked ₹1,664.00 daily-close stop?

epigraph.quote: Never add fresh capital to a stock trading below a flattening 50-day moving average with negative relative strength; trim Stage 3 exposure proactively and let a locked stop guard your core.
epigraph.author: Stan Weinstein Tape Discipline

web_blocks.html: Unlike our November 13 baseline in Stage 2 at ₹1,984.10, the tape has slipped into Stage 3 [27, 39]. On the verified 2026-11-23 NSE ledger, MANORAMA closed at ₹1,842.40 (-1.62% 1D, -5.89% 2W) [39]. That sits 14.74% below its ₹2,161.00 52-week high [39]. Price fell below its 20D SMA (₹1,889.12), flat 50D SMA (₹1,912.80), and 10W EMA (₹1,881.44) [39]. Daily RSI(14) cooled to 44.34 alongside 6 distribution days in 25 sessions [39].

web_blocks.takeaway: MANORAMA sits in Stage 3 (-2.43% vs 50D SMA, 4H turn false) with 6 distribution days. Raw TV support (₹1,597.01–₹1,645.65, stop ₹1,585.02) sits beneath our locked ₹1,664.00 daily-close stop, leaving no valid buy zone and reinforcing TRIM_OVERWEIGHT (sell 45 shares, hold 90 core).

web_blocks.html: Institutional ownership explains why the 30-week SMA (₹1,733.17) has not snapped yet. From June to September 2026, DIIs doubled their stake from 2.63% to 6.40% via the ₹500 crore QIP [1, 30]. FIIs also rose from 3.22% to 4.16% [1, 30]. The -2.94% dip in promoter stake (54.32% to 51.38%) came solely from QIP dilution, with zero promoter sales [1, 30]. Even so, 6 distribution days and -20.49% 28-day RS show institutions rotating out after the Nov 12 news, raising gap-down risk if we hold a full 5.83% weight untouched [32, 39].

Our options audit confirms MANORAMA is not in the NSE F&O segment (NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID) [31, 39]. There is no liquid call or put chain to hedge this Stage 3 pullback. All risk control must use cash-equity trimming (selling 45 of 135 shares now) and a locked daily-close hard stop on the 90 core shares.

web_blocks.title: Reconciling Raw TV Support (₹1,597–₹1,646) vs. Locked Upward-Only Stop (₹1,664.00)
paragraphs: Live TradingView's mechanical scanner flags nearest support at ₹1,597.01–₹1,645.65 (centered on Pivot S1 ₹1,621.33 and the 200-day SMA ₹1,619.19) with a raw invalidation stop at ₹1,585.02 [39]. We explicitly reconcile both levels against our November 13 baseline stop of ₹1,664.00. First, our upward-only stop-loss ratchet forbids lowering a held stop from ₹1,664.00 down to ₹1,585.02—especially because ₹1,664.00 aligns cleanly with the 63-day base low (₹1,660.80) just beneath the 40-week EMA (₹1,697.00). Second, because TradingView's raw support band (₹1,597.01–₹1,645.65) sits BELOW our locked ₹1,664.00 stop—and because capacity-bridged Base fair value is ₹1,800.00—we refuse to invent an intermediate watch zone above ₹1,664.00. Instead, new capital is REJECTED, we trim 45 shares now (TRIM_OVERWEIGHT), and a confirmed daily close below ₹1,664.00 triggers an automatic exit of all remaining 90 core shares.

book_paragraphs: Having re-audited the business and bridged our FY28E valuation target down to ₹1,800 in Chapter 7, you and I now turn to the tape—and the chart has changed meaningfully since mid-November. On November 13, Manorama sat cleanly in Stan Weinstein's Stage 2 above its 50-day moving average and 10-week EMA. Today, the stock has slipped into Stage 3 consolidation. That shift matters enormously: even when a company prints 41.9% year-on-year revenue growth, institutional portfolios do not add fresh capital—nor carry an untrimmed 5.83% position—while price is trapped beneath a flattening 50-day moving average and lagging the Nifty 50 by twenty percentage points over four weeks.

Let's keep our two market dates crystal clear so there is zero ambiguity. On the verified 2026-11-23 NSE ledger close—the session anchoring our Zerodha portfolio valuation—Manorama finished at ₹1,842.40, down 1.62% on the day and 14.74% below its 52-week high of ₹2,161.00. It traded below its 20-day SMA (₹1,889.12), below its flattening 50-day SMA (₹1,912.80), and below its approximate 10-week EMA (₹1,881.44), with daily RSI cooled to 44.34 and six distribution days logged across the prior 25 sessions. Relative strength tells the real institutional story: over 28 trading days, Manorama lagged the Nifty 50 by -20.49% (and -10.55% over 63 days).

Two days later, on the 2026-11-25 live TradingView snapshot, shares ticked up +0.95% to ₹1,859.90 on 140,757 shares—almost dead-on its 30-day average volume of 139,595 (1.01x). Does a +0.95% green day fix a Stage 3 chart? Not yet. At ₹1,859.90, Manorama still sits -1.45% below its 10-week EMA (₹1,887.31) and -2.43% below its 50-day SMA (₹1,906.21). Even on the 4-hour chart, the intraday turn signal remains false: 4-hour RSI sits at 44.41 (weaker than daily RSI at 45.97), and price remains pinned beneath both the 4-hour 20-period EMA (₹1,888.35) and 4-hour 50-period SMA (₹1,868.53). That is why TradingView's Stage 2 gate classifies the setup as STAGE_3 / CAP_WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT.

Yet notice what has not broken—and why a measured partial trim beats either stubborn inaction or panic liquidation. Manorama still trades +7.31% above its rising 30-week simple moving average (₹1,733.17), +9.60% above its 40-week EMA (₹1,697.00), and +14.87% above its 200-day SMA (₹1,619.19), with weekly RSI holding constructive neutral territory at 54.23. Trimming 45 of 135 shares near ₹1,842–₹1,860 cuts our Stage 3 weight from 5.83% to ~3.85%–3.89% while keeping 90 core shares alive if institutions defend the 30-week shelf.

book_subsections.title: Why the Tape Weakened After Strong Q2 Results
paragraphs: Retail investors are often baffled when a company posts +41.9% sales growth and +51.8% PAT growth, only for the stock to drift below its 50-day moving average. In Manorama's case, the tape is digesting two real things at once. First, after a 42.6% one-year rally and a June 2026 ₹500 crore QIP that doubled DII ownership from 2.63% to 6.40% (with FIIs up to 4.16%), short-term momentum money used Q2 earnings to lock in gains—creating six distribution days in 25 sessions.

Second, the November 12, 2026 Board announcement moving founders Ashish Ramesh Saraf and Vinita Ashish Saraf off the Board into non-board President roles while installing Deep Saraf as Managing Director and Mudit Kumar Singh as Chairman gave institutional committees a natural reason to pause. Add the ₹20.64 crore Customs deposit, promoter-owned Manorama Africa RPTs, and Burkina Faso's raw shea export levies, and carrying an untrimmed 5.83% weight in Stage 3 exposes the portfolio to unnecessary gap-down risk.

callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
callouts.text: When fundamentals say 'real compounder facing governance watchpoints and a ₹1,800 capacity-bridged ceiling' and the tape says 'Stage 3 with six distribution days,' you de-risk proactively. Trimming one-third of the position near flat cost frees cash for Stage 2 leaders while letting ₹1,664.00 guard the 90-share core.

book_subsections.title: Reconciling TradingView's Raw Support Band (₹1,597–₹1,646) Against Our Locked ₹1,664.00 Stop
paragraphs: One of the most important technical reconciliations in this refresh is resolving the gap between TradingView's raw scanner levels and our portfolio risk floor. On November 25, TradingView's automated technical screen placed MANORAMA's nearest support band at ₹1,597.01–₹1,645.65—anchored to Pivot S1 (₹1,621.33) and the 200-day SMA (₹1,619.19)—with a raw invalidation stop at ₹1,585.02. Meanwhile, our prior November 13 dossier had already locked our structural invalidation stop at ₹1,664.00.

Notice how our two rules resolve that tension cleanly with zero override gymnastics. First, our upward-only stop-loss ratchet strictly forbids moving a held position's stop downward from ₹1,664.00 to ₹1,585.02. Technically, ₹1,664.00 is also the sharper line in the sand: it sits right on the 63-day base low (₹1,660.80) and just 1.9% beneath the 40-week EMA (₹1,697.00), giving roughly 2.7 ATRs of room (at ₹72.62 14-day ATR, 3.90% daily volatility) before exiting ahead of a Stage 4 breakdown. Second, because TradingView's raw support band (₹1,597.01–₹1,645.65) sits BELOW our locked ₹1,664.00 stop—and because buying anywhere above ₹1,664.00 against our ₹1,800 Base Target offers less than 1.5:1 reward-to-risk—we refuse to invent an artificial buy zone above ₹1,664.00. New capital is simply REJECTED.

book_subsections.title: Cash-Equity Execution Without F&O Hedging
paragraphs: Because Manorama is not in the NSE F&O segment (NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID), we cannot sell covered calls to harvest Stage 3 theta or buy protective puts ahead of the postal ballot and Q3 FY27 earnings. All risk management lives in cash-equity position sizing and exact daily-close triggers.

That absence of options hedging makes our Stage 3 trim even more practical. Selling 45 of 135 shares near ₹1,842–₹1,860 immediately lowers our open stop risk from ₹26,446.50 (0.62% of NAV) down to ₹17,631.00 (0.41% of NAV) on the remaining 90 core shares—giving us clean, unemotional staying power behind our locked ₹1,664.00 daily-close hard stop.

book_subsections.title: Reading Distribution Days, Relative Strength & Future Re-Entry Criteria
paragraphs: When a stock slides into Stage 3, two quantitative gauges tell you whether institutions are quietly accumulating into weakness or actively rotating out: distribution-day clustering and multi-week relative strength against the Nifty 50. On the verified 2026-11-23 NSE ledger, Manorama carried six distribution days over the prior 25 sessions alongside a -20.49% 28-day relative strength reading and a -10.55% 63-day relative strength reading. That combination is why we refuse to treat a single +0.95% bounce to ₹1,859.90 on November 25 as an all-clear signal. Real institutional demand leaves footprints: tight daily closes, contracting Bollinger bandwidth (currently wide at 16.98%), and upside sessions that outpace the 30-day average volume of 139,595 shares.

What would eventually clear Manorama for fresh capital in a future refresh? Not an arbitrary bounce inside Stage 3, but two simultaneous conditions: first, a decisive Stage 2 base resolution reclaiming both the 10-week EMA (₹1,887.31) and 50-day SMA (₹1,906.21) on heavy volume with distribution days rolling off; and second, an upward earnings/capacity reset (from on-time Solvent Fractionation-3 execution and clean March 2027 H2 debt liquidation) or a deeper valuation reset that restores at least 1.5:1 reward-to-risk against our peer-aligned 35x multiple. Until both trend and valuation align, fresh capital stays out while 90 core shares ride behind ₹1,664.00.
